nodes.name: server_users_search
nodes.task: Implement the users search endpoint in server/users.ts, following the published contract at contracts/users.json exactly: GET /users with query params q (string filter matching against user name/id) and optional cursor; response body { items: [{ id: string, name: string }], nextCursor: string | null }. Return 400 for an invalid/unrecognized cursor and 500 for an unexpected internal error, as the contract's errors map specifies. Preserve the contract's stated defaults (cursor pagination with nextCursor null on the last page) and keep the q filter semantics simple and documented; if an edge case (e.g. empty q, case sensitivity) is undefined by the contract, pick a reasonable behavior and document it in a comment. Add server-side unit tests covering filtering, pagination advance/termination, the 400 invalid-cursor path, and the 500 path (via an injected failure if the implementation allows one). Project conventions: TypeScript ESM (package.json "type": "module"), tests run with `node --test`; README lists server/users.ts as the endpoint source. Do not modify contracts/users.json or package.json.

nodes.name: web_users_search
nodes.task: Implement the browser users search UI in web/users.ts, targeting the GET /users endpoint contract in contracts/users.json: query params q and optional cursor; response { items: [{ id, name }], nextCursor: string | null }. Requirements: debounced search input (debounce a short, configurable interval; cancel/replace pending timers on new input), cursor-based "load more" pagination using nextCursor, explicit loading, empty, and error states (error state should surface 400/500 failures from the endpoint), and stale-response protection so a slower earlier request cannot overwrite the results of a newer query or page (e.g. request token/sequence check before applying state). No UI framework is required (README: web/users.ts is the browser source; note the existing mountUsers(element) entry point may be reshaped). Fetch calls should go through an injectable/mockable request function so browser-level unit tests can run in a DOM-free or minimal-DOM harness with a stubbed fetch. Add unit tests for debounce behavior, state transitions (loading/empty/error), pagination flow, and the out-of-order/stale-response guard. Project conventions: TypeScript ESM, `node --test` runner. Do not modify contracts/users.json or package.json.

nodes.name: users_flow_acceptance
nodes.task: Add integrated acceptance coverage in tests/users-flow.test.ts that exercises the browser users search flow (web/users.ts) against the real server endpoint implemented in server/users.ts. Required scenarios: a q-filtered search returning matching users; cursor pagination walking pages to exhaustion with nextCursor null; an invalid cursor producing the contract's 400 error and a visible error state in the UI; and an out-of-order/stale-response scenario where responses arrive in reverse order and the UI ends up showing only the newest query's results. Follow the contract in contracts/users.json as the source of truth for request/response shape and error semantics. Run the full test suite with `node --test` (per package.json scripts.test) and confirm all server unit tests, web unit tests, and this integration suite pass. Verify that contracts/users.json and package.json are byte-for-byte unchanged. If acceptance checks fail, report rejection to the owning implementation nodes (server_users_search or web_users_search) with the specific failing evidence; do not rewrite their implementation code yourself except for fixing the integration test harness itself. Output a concise acceptance report: conclusion, exact commands run with exit codes, test counts, and links to detailed evidence saved in the repository.

originalGoal: Deliver users search using the existing immutable contracts/users.json contract. Implement server/users.ts with q filtering, cursor pagination and the specified 400/500 errors, and server unit tests. Implement web/users.ts with debounced search, pagination, loading/empty/error states and protection against stale responses, with browser unit tests. Add integrated acceptance coverage in tests/users-flow.test.ts exercising the browser against the endpoint, including invalid cursors and out-of-order responses. Keep the published contract and package manifest unchanged.
